exercises.name: Jar Opening
description: Sit facing the table with back supported and both feet flat
Both hands share the task
The affected hand grips the lid or cap using a cylindrical or spherical grasp
The unaffected hand stabilizes the jar
Practice rotation of the wrist while twisting the lid or cap
Start with loosely fitted lids and progress to tighter ones
Once open, release the lid with controlled movement
Repeat with different containers
Progression: move from large wide lids (easy) to smaller narrower caps (more challenging)
Repeat 6–10 opening/closing attempts, 2–3 sets, 8–12 minutes

exercises.name: Dish Washing
description: Sit upright with feet supported and trunk stable
The affected hand is the manipulator (holds sponge and scrubs) and the unaffected hand is the stabilizer (holds bowl or plate); encourage progressive affected-hand use
Start with small items (2 cups, 2 plates, 2 spoons)
Place plate or bowl at midline and sponge within easy reach of the affected hand
Unaffected hand holds and stabilizes the plate on the table
Affected hand grasps the sponge using palmar grasp with active finger flexion and wrist movement
Perform circular or back-and-forth scrubbing movements on the plate
Both hands coordinate to rotate or slide the plate to clean different areas
Encourage smooth, controlled bilateral movements
Place the plate aside and repeat
Repeat 5–10 items, 10 minutes per session
exercises.items: Sponge or soft scrub brush, table, chair, utensils (plate, cups, spoon)

exercises.name: Paper Smoothing
description: Sit upright with feet flat and the affected arm resting on the table
Crumpled paper is placed in front of the patient
Place the palm or fingers of the affected hand on the crumpled paper
The unaffected hand stabilizes the paper
Press the paper flat with the palm
Slide the hand over the paper to stretch and flatten it forward, sideways, or diagonally
Encourage long, slow strokes with even pressure
Reposition the hand on another wrinkled section and repeat the smoothing motion until most wrinkles are flattened
Lift the hand, rest briefly, and repeat for the next set
Repeat 8–10 smoothing strokes per attempt, 3 sets, 5–7 minutes total
exercises.dosage: 8–10 smoothing strokes per attempt, 3 sets, 5–7 minutes total
exercises.items: Crumpled paper, stable table at elbow height, chair with back support

exercises.name: Namaste Position
description: Sit upright with hips and knees at 90 degrees, feet flat, and trunk supported
Hands start on the lap at waist height
Bring both hands toward the midline with palms aligned facing each other
Gently place both palms together in front of the chest in the Namaste position
Extend and align fingers as much as possible with wrists remaining neutral
Gently press both palms together with equal pressure from both hands, emphasizing activation of the affected hand
Maintain the Namaste position for 5–10 seconds, focusing on symmetry and steady posture
Slowly separate the hands and return to resting position
Repeat for the prescribed number of repetitions
Repeat 8–12 reps, hold 5–8 seconds, 2–3 sets, 1 session/day
exercises.items: Chair with back support (optional: mirror for visual feedback)

exercises.name: Pouring Water
description: Sit upright with feet flat, hips and knees at 90 degrees, and table at elbow height
Glass placed at midline; bottle placed within comfortable reach on the affected side
Unaffected hand places the palm or fingers around the base of the glass to steady it, kept on an absorbent mat
Using the affected hand, take a secure cylindrical grasp around the bottle with wrist neutral
Lift the bottle 5–10 cm off the table using elbow and shoulder control
Bring the bottle above the centre of the glass rim
Slowly tilt the bottle to allow a small, controlled stream into the glass; hold the tilt for 1–3 seconds
Slowly bring the bottle back to vertical and lower it to the table
Open fingers to release the bottle and rest
Repeat 8–12 reps, 3 sets, 1–2 sessions/day
exercises.items: Lightweight plastic bottle (start empty or with very small volume), glass or wide-rim cup, table at elbow height, chair with back support, towel or absorbent mat

exercises.name: Knot Opening
description: Sit upright with feet flat and forearm supported on the table
A towel with a knot is placed at midline or slightly toward the affected side
Hold one end of the towel in each hand, ensuring both hands are actively involved
Visually locate the knot and bring both hands closer to it
Using bilateral coordinated movements, manipulate the towel by: pulling the towel ends in opposite directions, twisting or rotating the towel, and adjusting finger placement to loosen the knot
The affected hand takes an active role in stabilizing, pulling, and manipulating the towel rather than being passive
Continue manipulating until the knot is completely opened
Once opened, reset the towel and repeat
Perform in a controlled, purposeful manner, avoiding excessive speed or compensatory trunk movements
Repeat 6–8 reps, 1–2 sets, once daily
exercises.items: Towel, table, chair with back support

exercises.name: Wear and Remove Wrist watch
description: Sit upright with hips and knees at 90 degrees, feet flat, trunk supported, and forearm on the table at comfortable height (elbow 60–90 degrees)

Donning (putting on watch): pick up the watch using both hands; position the watch face over the wrist; the unaffected hand stabilizes the watch face and strap while the affected hand guides the free end of the strap through the buckle; align the strap holes and insert the pin into the appropriate hole using controlled finger movements; thread the strap end through the keeper loop to secure the watch

Doffing (removing watch): use the unaffected hand to stabilize the wrist and watch face; the affected hand disengages the strap from the keeper loop; carefully release the pin from the strap hole; loosen the strap and remove the watch using bilateral coordinated movements
Place the watch back on the table in an organized manner
Repeat 6–8 don/doff cycles, 1 set, once daily
exercises.items: Watch with buckle fastening, chair with back support, table

exercises.name: Battery Changing
description: Sit upright with feet flat, trunk supported, and forearm on the table
Ensure good lighting and place the device at midline on the table
Hold the device steady with the unaffected hand
Open the battery cover using the affected hand (slide, press, or twist depending on the device)
Take out old batteries one by one and place them safely in a container
Look at the + and – signs inside the device
Put new batteries in the same direction (spring end touches the flat end of the battery)
Close the cover until it clicks or screws tight
Test the device (press button or switch on flashlight)
Repeat the task
Repeat 3–4 times (open → remove → insert → close), 1 session per day

exercises.name: Lock and Key
description: Sit upright with feet flat and forearm supported on the table so the wrist and fingers do the work
Lock placed at comfortable midline height (table level)
Place the lock on the table with the keyhole facing you
Pick a large, easy key and hold it between thumb and index finger
Use the non-affected hand to hold the lock steady
Look at the key and keyhole; line up the key's teeth the correct way
Gently push the key straight into the keyhole
Rotate the key slowly in the required direction until it turns (lock or unlock) using wrist rotation and finger pinch — avoid large shoulder movement
Rotate back to starting position
Pull the key straight out with a controlled pinch
Reinsert and repeat the full cycle
Repeat 5 full cycles (insert → turn → return → remove), 1 set, once daily
exercises.dosage: 5 full cycles (insert → turn → return → remove) × 1 set, once daily
exercises.items: Practice lock set, large easy-to-hold keys, chair with back support, table

exercises.name: Colouring or Dot-to-Dot
description: Sit upright on a chair with feet supported, in front of the table
Paper is placed on the table at midline
Colouring activity: select a colouring tool based on hand strength and grip
Use the affected hand to colour within boundaries
Encourage slow, controlled strokes, filling sections one by one
Promote use of the unaffected hand for stabilizing the sheet
Dot-to-dot activity: the patient receives a numbered dot-to-dot worksheet
Connect dots in sequential order (1-2-3…)
Use a pencil or pen, keeping the wrist stable and motion smooth
After forming the image, optionally colour the final picture
Repeat: Colouring — 2 sets of 2–3 large simple shapes; Dot-to-dot — 2 sets of 2–3 simple dot patterns (5–10 dots)
exercises.dosage: Colouring: 2 sets × 2–3 reps; Dot-to-dot: 2 sets × 2–3 reps
exercises.items: Colouring sheets (simple to complex patterns), dot-to-dot worksheets, crayons or colour pencils or markers, pencil or pen, chair, table
